mainTopic: The scope of the false-prophet dispute, the עדים זוממין of a בת כהן, and the opening of פרק חלק on who loses עולם הבא.
overview: The amud starts by working out which false-prophet cases fall under the dispute between רבי שמעון (חנק) and the חכמים (סקילה). The first view, defended by רב חסדא against רב המנונא's challenge, limits the dispute to עבודה זרה, whether the prophet uproots it fully or cancels only part. רב המנונא says the dispute also covers fully uprooting any מצוה. A ברייתא on the topic is then read two ways: אביי reads it like רב חסדא, and רבא reads it like רב המנונא. רבי יוחנן gives the practical rule: listen to a prophet's temporary order to break any מצוה except עבודה זרה, even if he stops the sun. רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא discuss how such a miracle could happen. Next, a ברייתא of רבי יוסי teaches that the עדים זוממין of a בת כהן get the man's חנק, because the פסוק says 'his brother'. The פרק ends, and פרק חלק opens: all of ישראל have a share in עולם הבא, except those the משנה lists. The גמרא explains that one who denies תחיית המתים loses it מדה כנגד מדה, and starts a proof from אלישע's prophecy that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute is only about idol worship, even partial
steps.stepSummary: The dispute between רבי שמעון and the חכמים applies to a prophet who uproots עבודה זרה completely, or who cancels only part of it. The source is ״מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ״, which means even part of the way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument is about a prophet who wipes out the איסור of עבודה זרה completely, or who keeps part of it and cancels part of it. That is because the Torah says 'from the way,' which means even from part of the way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is defining exactly which cases the dispute between רבי שמעון (חנק) and the חכמים (סקילה) is about. The answer is two cases, both involving עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases are included: uprooting עבודה זרה entirely, and partly allowing it. The partial case counts as well because the פסוק says ״מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ״, 'from the way,' which is read as even a piece of the way.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute; here, the argument between רבי שמעון and the חכמים about which death penalty applies
Uprooting the essence, meaning cancelling a מצוה completely
Keeping part and cancelling part, meaning a partial cancellation
Idol worship
'The Merciful One', a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: The dispute here is not about whether he is punished at all, since both sides agree he gets the death penalty. They only argue about which death: סקילה (the חכמים) or חנק (רבי שמעון).

phrases.english: The dispute is about [a prophet who] uproots the essence of idol worship,
phrases.notes: 'Uproots the essence' means he claims the whole איסור is cancelled, not just part of it.

phrases.aramaic: וְקִיּוּם מִקְצָת וּבִיטּוּל מִקְצָת דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: and [one who says to] keep part and cancel part of idol worship,
for the Merciful One said: "from the way"
phrases.notes: דברים 13:6

phrases.english: even [from] part of the way.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּעוֹקֵר הַגּוּף דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by defining the scope of the earlier dispute between רבי שמעון and the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between חנק and סקילה applies to a prophet who uproots עבודה זרה fully, or who cancels part of it, based on ״מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ״.

steps.title: For other מצוות, everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: For other מצוות, uprooting a whole מצוה gets חנק according to everyone. Cancelling only part of one carries no punishment according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if a prophet wipes out a different מצוה completely, everyone agrees he gets חנק. If he keeps part and cancels part of a different מצוה, everyone agrees he is not punished.
steps.whatsHappening: The same statement continues and explains what happens with all the other מצוות, where there is no dispute at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the contrast to עבודה זרה. With other מצוות, a partial cancellation is not punished at all, and a full uprooting is punished only with חנק. The extra seriousness of the חכמים' view (סקילה), and liability for partial cancellation, apply only to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The rest of the מצוות, meaning all the מצוות other than עבודה זרה
Everyone agrees
Strangulation, one of the four court death penalties
Exempt, meaning not punished

steps.whatToRemember: According to this first view, the dispute is about עבודה זרה only: uprooting it fully or partly. For other מצוות, everyone agrees that a full uprooting gets חנק and a partial cancellation is פטור.

phrases.english: But [one who] uproots the essence of the other מצוות,
everyone agrees [he is killed] by strangulation.

phrases.aramaic: וְקִיּוּם מִקְצָת וּבִיטּוּל מִקְצָת דְּבִשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת,
phrases.english: And [one who says to] keep part and cancel part of the other מצוות,
everyone agrees he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל עוֹקֵר הַגּוּף דִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the same statement by giving the contrast case of the other מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For other מצוות, everyone agrees: a full uprooting gets חנק, and a partial cancellation is פטור.

steps.title: How can there be a positive מצוה about idol worship?
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא challenges the first view from a teaching on the פסוק. It says ״לָלֶכֶת״ refers to a מצוות עשה and ״בָּהּ״ refers to a לא תעשה. He asks what positive מצוה exists about עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא objects: A teaching says 'to walk' means a מצוות עשה, and 'in it' means a לא תעשה. If the פסוק is only about עבודה זרה, how could there be a מצוות עשה about עבודה זרה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא attacks the idea that the פסוק of the false prophet speaks only about עבודה זרה. A ברייתא learns from the same פסוק that it includes a positive מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the prophet is liable for drawing people away from both a מצוות עשה and a לא תעשה. עבודה זרה seems to be only a prohibition (don't worship idols). So the mention of an עשה suggests the פסוק covers other מצוות as well, which would contradict the first view.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection, usually from an earlier source such as a ברייתא
A positive commandment, meaning something you must do
A negative commandment, meaning a prohibition
If you think that... (introduces an assumption the speaker is about to show is a problem)
How can you find it? (how is such a case possible?)

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna raises an objection:
"To walk": this is a positive מצוה,
phrases.notes: These words come from the same פסוק as before: 'the way in which ה׳ commanded you to walk' (דברים 13:6).

phrases.english: "In it": this is a negative מצוה.
And if it enters your mind [that the verse is] about idol worship [only],

phrases.aramaic: עֲשֵׂה בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ?
phrases.english: a positive מצוה in idol worship, how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim from steps 1 and 2 that the פסוק and the dispute are limited to עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the false prophet's פסוק, and the dispute based on it, deal only with עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא learns a מצוות עשה from the פסוק. עבודה זרה seems to have no positive מצוה, so the פסוק must include other מצוות.

steps.title: The positive מצוה is smashing idols
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that there is a מצוות עשה connected to עבודה זרה: ״וְנִתַּצְתֶּם״, the command to smash idolatrous altars.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא explained it: [the positive מצוה is] 'and you shall smash [their altars].'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defends the first view by pointing to a positive מצוה that is about עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed there is no עשה involving עבודה זרה. רב חסדא shows there is one: the Torah commands us to destroy idols and their altars. A prophet who says not to destroy them is pulling people away from an עשה of עבודה זרה, so the פסוק can still be only about עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, meaning he gave an interpretation that solves the problem
'And you shall smash', the command to destroy idolatrous altars

phrases.english: Rav Chisda explained it: "And you shall smash."
phrases.notes: דברים 12:3

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב המנונא's challenge by naming a מצוות עשה connected to עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a fact the challenger missed: such an עשה does exist.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עבודה זרה has only prohibitions, so the ברייתא's עשה must refer to other מצוות.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״וְנִתַּצְתֶּם״ is a positive מצוה about עבודה זרה, so the פסוק can be limited to עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רב המנונא's own version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא says the dispute covers uprooting any מצוה completely, whether עבודה זרה or other מצוות. It also covers partial cancelling of עבודה זרה, based on ״מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא says: The argument is about a prophet who wipes out a מצוה completely, whether it is עבודה זרה or other מצוות. It is also about one who keeps part and cancels part of עבודה זרה. That is because the Torah says 'from the way,' which means even part of the way.
steps.whatsHappening: His challenge was answered, but רב המנונא now gives a different way of drawing the lines of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change is in one case: fully uprooting other מצוות. The first view said everyone agrees it gets חנק. רב המנונא puts it inside the dispute, so the חכמים would say סקילה. Partial cancelling still counts only for עבודה זרה, using the same source ״מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ״.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether... or... (both cases are included)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views. The first, defended by רב חסדא, limits the dispute to עבודה זרה (full or partial). רב המנונא expands it to a full uprooting of any מצוה, while partial cancelling still counts only for עבודה זרה.
steps.confusionAlert: רב המנונא repeats ״מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ״, but the repetition only covers partial cancelling of עבודה זרה. It is not his source for including other מצוות.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:
The dispute is about [a prophet who] uproots the essence [of a מצוה],

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בֵּין בִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת,
phrases.english: whether with idol worship or with the other מצוות,

phrases.aramaic: וְקִיּוּם מִקְצָת וּבִיטּוּל מִקְצָת דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: and [one who says to] keep part and cancel part of idol worship.
For the Merciful One said: "from the way,"
even [from] part of the way.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הַמְנוּנָא אָמַר: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בְּעוֹקֵר הַגּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his objection is answered, רב המנונא offers a different definition of what the dispute covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between חנק and סקילה covers a full uprooting of any מצוה, plus partial cancelling of עבודה זרה.

steps.title: End of רב המנונא's view: partial cancelling of other מצוות is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא finishes his statement: if a prophet keeps part and cancels part of a regular מצוה (not עבודה זרה), everyone agrees he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he says to keep part of a regular מצוה and cancel part of it, everyone agrees he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב המנונא's statement from the previous step. It tells us the one case that is outside the dispute: partly cancelling an ordinary מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רב המנונא widened the dispute to cover fully uprooting any מצוה, and also partly cancelling עבודה זרה. Here he sets the limit: partly cancelling any other מצוה is not punished by anyone. So his map has three zones: fully uprooting any מצוה is disputed, partly cancelling עבודה זרה is disputed, and partly cancelling other מצוות is exempt for all.

keyTerms.meaning: keeping part (of a מצוה)
cancelling part (of a מצוה)
the other מצוות (not עבודה זרה)
everyone agrees
exempt from punishment

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב המנונא, only one case is exempt for everyone: partly cancelling a מצוה that is not עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: But keeping part and cancelling part,
that is, with the other מצוות,
everyone agrees he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל קִיּוּם מִקְצָת וּבִיטּוּל מִקְצָת, דְּבִשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב המנונא's statement from step 5 by naming the case that falls outside the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Partly cancelling a מצוה other than עבודה זרה gets no punishment, according to everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a prophet who uproots or partly cancels Torah laws
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches three rulings. A prophet who uproots a Torah law is liable. If he keeps part and cancels part, רבי שמעון exempts him. For עבודה זרה, even 'serve it today, cancel it tomorrow' makes him liable according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A prophet who comes to uproot something from the Torah is liable. If he says to keep part and cancel part, רבי שמעון exempts him. With עבודה זרה, even if he says 'Serve it today and cancel it tomorrow', everyone agrees he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on our topic. It is setting up the next move, where אביי and רבא will each read it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not fully clear. It does not say who holds the first ruling (liable for uprooting), or what the חכמים say about partial cancelling. Those open points let both רב חסדא's view and רב המנונא's view try to fit it, which is why the next steps explain it two ways.

keyTerms.meaning: the Rabbis taught (opens a ברייתא)
one who prophesies
to uproot something from the Torah
liable (to the death penalty)
exempts

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: הַמִּתְנַבֵּא לַעֲקוֹר דָּבָר מִן הַתּוֹרָה – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: One who prophesies to uproot something from the Torah is liable.
To keep part and cancel part:
רבי שמעון exempts him.
And with עבודה זרה, even if he says:
'Serve it today and cancel it tomorrow,'
everyone agrees he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמִּתְנַבֵּא לַעֲקוֹר דָּבָר מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that both sides of the earlier discussion will now have to explain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Uprooting a Torah law makes the prophet liable. רבי שמעון exempts partial cancelling. For עבודה זרה, even partial cancelling makes him liable according to everyone.

steps.title: אביי follows רב חסדא, רבא follows רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says אביי holds like רב חסדא and reads the ברייתא his way, while רבא holds like רב המנונא and reads it his way.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי holds like רב חסדא and explains the ברייתא like רב חסדא. רבא holds like רב המנונא and explains it like רב המנונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us which later אמורא follows which earlier view. It is setting up the next steps, where each reading of the ברייתא will be spelled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of them does two things. 'סבר לה' means he agrees with that view. 'ומתרץ לה' means he also explains the ברייתא so it fits that view. So the ברייתא does not prove either side, because both can read it their own way.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds it (agrees with this view)
he explains it (reads the ברייתא to fit)

phrases.english: אביי holds like רב חסדא,
phrases.notes: רב חסדא's view is the first one: the dispute applies only to עבודה זרה (steps 1-4).

phrases.english: and explains it (the ברייתא) like רב חסדא.
רבא holds like רב המנונא,
and explains it like רב המנונא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב חִסְדָּא, וּמְתָרֵץ לַהּ כְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assigns the two earlier views to אביי and רבא, and announces that each will read the ברייתא his own way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי follows רב חסדא and רבא follows רב המנונא, each reading the ברייתא to fit his view.

steps.title: אביי reads the ברייתא according to רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the ברייתא this way. Uprooting any Torah law gets חנק according to everyone. Partial cancelling is exempt according to everyone. For עבודה זרה, even partial cancelling is liable, and each side keeps its own death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי holds like רב חסדא and explains the ברייתא like רב חסדא. A prophet who uproots something from the Torah gets חנק according to everyone. If he says to keep part and cancel part, רבי שמעון exempts him, and so do the רבנן. With עבודה זרה, even if he said 'Serve it today and cancel it tomorrow', he is liable. Each Sage follows his own view about which death penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the line about אביי and now spells out his reading of the ברייתא, line by line. It fills in the gaps the ברייתא left open so it fits רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי reads the first ruling ('liable') as everyone agreeing on חנק, because for ordinary מצוות there is no dispute. He says the רבנן also exempt partial cancelling, and רבי שמעון is named only as one example. For עבודה זרה, 'everyone agrees he is liable' means everyone agrees he dies. They still argue about how: the רבנן say סקילה and רבי שמעון says חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: strangulation (one of the death penalties of בית דין)
and the same rule applies
each Sage follows his own view

steps.confusionAlert: 'Everyone agrees he is liable' for עבודה זרה does not mean everyone agrees on the same punishment. They agree he gets the death penalty, but each side keeps its own type of death.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי (following רב חסדא), the dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן is only about which death penalty a prophet of עבודה זרה gets. For ordinary מצוות, uprooting gets חנק for everyone and partial cancelling is exempt for everyone.

phrases.english: אביי holds like רב חסדא,
and explains it like רב חסדא:
One who prophesies to uproot something from the Torah:
everyone agrees he is put to death by חנק.
To keep part and cancel part:
רבי שמעון exempts him,
and the same is true for the רבנן.
And with עבודה זרה, even if he said
'Serve it today and cancel it tomorrow,' he is liable.

phrases.aramaic: מָר כִּדְאִית לֵיהּ, וּמַר כִּדְאִית לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: One Sage follows his view, and the other Sage follows his view.
phrases.notes: He means the type of death: the רבנן say סקילה (stoning), and רבי שמעון says חנק.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב חִסְדָּא, וּמְתָרֵץ לַהּ כְּרַב חִסְדָּא: הַמִּתְנַבֵּא לַעֲקוֹר דָּבָר מִן הַתּוֹרָה – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל בְּחֶנֶק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first of the two readings announced in step 8, the one that follows רב חסדא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the ברייתא so it fits רב חסדא's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: You might think the ברייתא's 'liable' and 'רבי שמעון exempts' show a dispute about ordinary מצוות, which would fit רב המנונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read according to רב חסדא, there is no dispute about ordinary מצוות. The disagreement is only about which death penalty applies for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבא reads the ברייתא according to רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the ברייתא his way. Uprooting any מצוה fully makes the prophet liable. Partial cancelling of a regular מצוה is exempt according to everyone. For עבודה זרה, even partial cancelling makes him liable. In the liable cases, each side keeps its own death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא agrees with רב המנונא and explains the ברייתא like him. A prophet who says to uproot a Torah law, whether about עבודה זרה or any other מצוה, is liable, and each side gives its own death penalty. If he says to keep part and cancel part of a regular מצוה, רבי שמעון exempts him, and the רבנן agree. About עבודה זרה, even if he says 'serve it today, cancel it tomorrow,' he is liable, and each side gives its own death penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other half of what step 8 promised. After אביי's reading in step 9, the גמרא now shows how רבא fits the same ברייתא into רב המנונא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the argument between רבי שמעון and the רבנן is about which death penalty applies (סקילה or חנק), not about whether the prophet is liable. So in every liable case the ברייתא means 'liable, each side with his own penalty.' When the ברייתא names only רבי שמעון as exempting for partial cancelling, רבא says the רבנן agree too.

keyTerms.meaning: explains it (fits the ברייתא into his view)

keyTerms.term: מָר כִּדְאִית לֵיהּ וּמָר כִּדְאִית לֵיהּ
keyTerms.meaning: each master according to his own view
and the same rule applies
to keep part and cancel part

steps.whatToRemember: אביי and רבא read the same ברייתא in two ways. אביי (like רב חסדא) says uprooting a regular מצוה is חנק according to everyone. רבא (like רב המנונא) says the two sides argue about the penalty even there.
steps.confusionAlert: Both readings agree on who is liable and who is exempt. They differ only on which death penalty applies to fully uprooting a regular מצוה.

phrases.english: Rava holds like Rav Hamnuna,
and explains it like Rav Hamnuna:
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא from step 7.

phrases.english: One who prophesies to uproot a matter from the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בֵּין בִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: whether about idol worship or about the other מצוות, is liable,

phrases.aramaic: מָר כִּדְאִית לֵיהּ וּמַר כִּדְאִית לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: this master as he holds, and that master as he holds.
phrases.notes: The רבנן give סקילה, and רבי שמעון gives חנק.

phrases.aramaic: לְקַיֵּים מִקְצָת וּלְבַטֵּל מִקְצָת בִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת –
phrases.english: To keep part and cancel part, in the other מצוות:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹטֵר, וְהוּא הַדִּין לְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon exempts him, and the same is true for the Rabbis.
And with idol worship, even if he says,
"Serve it today and cancel it tomorrow," he is liable,

phrases.aramaic: מָר כִּדְאִית לֵיהּ וּמַר כִּדְאִית לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: this master as he holds, and that master as he holds.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב הַמְנוּנָא, וּמְתָרֵץ לַהּ כְּרַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of the two readings promised in step 8, alongside אביי's reading in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא to fit an אמורא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא names only רבי שמעון as exempting partial cancelling, and its 'דברי הכל חייב' about עבודה זרה seems to mean one agreed penalty.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבא, everyone exempts partial cancelling of regular מצוות. In every liable case, each side keeps its own death penalty.

steps.title: Obey a prophet in everything except idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that if a proven prophet says to break a Torah law, you listen to him. The exception is עבודה זרה: even a sun-stopping miracle does not let you listen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: In everything, if a prophet tells you to break the words of the Torah, listen to him. The exception is עבודה זרה. Even if he makes the sun stand still in the middle of the sky, do not listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a summary rule about when a prophet may be obeyed. A prophet can tell you to break a מצוה for now, but never to serve עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the ברייתא above. A temporary order about a regular מצוה is allowed, but about עבודה זרה nothing is allowed, not even 'serve it today, cancel it tomorrow.' Even the strongest proof of being a prophet cannot permit עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: transgress the words of the Torah
listen to him
the sun in the middle of the sky

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for a prophet's temporary orders. A true prophet can suspend a מצוה for a time, as אליהו did with his offering on הר הכרמל, but never for עבודה זרה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
In everything, if a prophet tells you,
"Transgress the words of the Torah," listen to him,
phrases.notes: He means breaking it for now, not uprooting it forever. Uprooting a law makes the prophet liable, as we just learned.

phrases.english: except for idol worship,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ מַעֲמִיד לְךָ חַמָּה בְּאֶמְצַע הָרָקִיעַ –
phrases.english: for even if he stops the sun for you in the middle of the sky,
do not listen to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּכֹּל, אִם יֹאמַר לְךָ נָבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the special strictness about עבודה זרה from the ברייתא into a practical rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Listen to a prophet's temporary order to break any מצוה except עבודה זרה, no matter what miracle he shows.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: the Torah knew idol worship's pull
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי supports the same rule. The Torah understood how strong עבודה זרה's pull is, so it warns: even if the prophet stops the sun, do not listen.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי הגלילי says: The Torah understood the full depth of עבודה זרה. That is why it gave it power. So even if he stops the sun for you in the middle of the sky, do not listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי יוחנן. It adds the reason why even a huge miracle does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah knew that a prophet of עבודה זרה might really show wonders, so it told us ahead of time not to be fooled. A real miracle is no proof at all when the message is עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: the Torah reached the very end of its mind (fully understood it)
power, control
therefore

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:

phrases.aramaic: הִגִּיעָה תּוֹרָה לְסוֹף דַּעְתָּהּ שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: The Torah reached the very end of the mind of idol worship,
phrases.notes: In other words, the Torah knew exactly how strong the pull of עבודה זרה is.

phrases.english: therefore the Torah gave it power,
phrases.notes: The Torah admits that a prophet of עבודה זרה could actually perform wonders.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ מַעֲמִיד לְךָ חַמָּה בְּאֶמְצַע הָרָקִיעַ –
phrases.english: so that even if he stops the sun for you in the middle of the sky,
do not listen to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's rule with a ברייתא and explains its reasoning.
steps.raayaObject: Even a sun-stopping miracle does not allow listening to a prophet about עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: God would not do miracles for idolaters
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the idea that God would let a prophet of עבודה זרה do a real miracle. The warning is about someone like חנניה בן עזור, who began as a true prophet and later became false.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי עקיבא said: Heaven forbid that the Holy One, Blessed be He, would stop the sun for those who go against His will! Rather, the case is like חנניה בן עזור, who was a true prophet at first and a false prophet in the end.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back against the idea that a prophet of עבודה זרה could do a real miracle. He explains that the verse is talking about someone who earned his miracles back when he was still a true prophet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי allowed that עבודה זרה's prophet might really show wonders. רבי עקיבא says God never does that for people who rebel against Him. So the miracle came while the prophet was still true, and once he calls for עבודה זרה he is false, whatever his past record.

keyTerms.meaning: Heaven forbid
those who go against His will
a prophet who started out true and became false
false prophet

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Akiva said:
Heaven forbid that the Holy One, Blessed be He,
would stop the sun for those who go against His will!
Rather, it means someone like Chananiah son of Azzur,
phrases.notes: His story is in ירמיהו 28.

phrases.english: who at first was a true prophet,
and in the end a false prophet.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes how רבי יוסי הגלילי understood the miracle, while agreeing with the rule not to listen.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the idea that God gives miracles to a prophet of עבודה זרה. The rule 'do not listen' stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: God would not stop the sun for people who rebel against Him. Any miracle must come from the prophet's earlier time as a true prophet.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees: about עבודה זרה, never listen, even after a miracle. רבי עקיבא only adds that such a miracle comes from the prophet's past as a true prophet, like חנניה בן עזור.

steps.title: Source for the plotting witnesses of a בת כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which says the עדים זוממין of a בת כהן get חנק, and asks where this comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that the עדים זוממין of a בת כהן get חנק. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בת כהן who sins with another man gets שריפה, a harsher death. Normally עדים זוממין get whatever they tried to do to the accused. So it is surprising that these witnesses get only חנק, and the גמרא wants a source.

keyTerms.meaning: plotting witnesses (עדים זוממין)
the daughter of a כהן
from where do we know these words?

phrases.english: And the plotting witnesses of a kohen's daughter:
From where do we know these words?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזוֹמְמֵי בַּת כֹּהֵן – מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of prophets and turns to the next item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that the עדים זוממין of a בת כהן get חנק and not her שריפה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: plotting witnesses match the man's penalty
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא answers with a ברייתא of רבי יוסי. It opens with a general rule: in all the Torah's cases of עדים זוממין against a woman, the witnesses and the man with her get the same penalty as she does. The next step shows why a בת כהן is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא said: As it was taught, רבי יוסי says: What does the פסוק 'And you shall do to him as he plotted to do to his brother' come to teach? It teaches that in all cases in the Torah of people plotted against, their plotting witnesses and their partners get the same penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the answer to the question in step 14. A ברייתא first sets out the normal rule for עדים זוממין in cases of forbidden relations. The next step shows how the בת כהן case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the woman, the man with her, and the witnesses who falsely accused them all get the same death penalty. This general rule sets up the problem of a בת כהן, where the woman and the man get different deaths. The ברייתא solves that problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: what does the פסוק come to teach?
as he plotted
the men who were with them
the same as them

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Ika said:
As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
What does the verse come to teach,
"And you shall do to him as he plotted to do to his brother"?
phrases.notes: דברים 19:19

phrases.english: Because in all the cases in the Torah of people plotted against,
their plotting witnesses and the men with them are treated like them.
phrases.notes: 'Like them' means like the woman. Usually she, the man, and the false witnesses all get the same death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי's ברייתא on 'as he plotted to do to his brother' supplies the answer. Normally the witnesses and the man match the woman's penalty. In a בת כהן case, 'to his brother' (step 16) matches the witnesses to the man, so they get חנק.
steps.whatToRemember: The עדים זוממין of a בת כהן get חנק, like the man, not שריפה like her. The source is רבי יוסי's reading of 'to his brother.'

steps.title: The plotting witnesses get the man's punishment, not the woman's
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes. A בת כהן is the exception, because she gets שריפה while the man gets חנק. 'To his brother, and not to his sister' shows the עדים זוממין get his punishment, which is חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בת כהן is punished by burning, but the man with her is not. For the plotting witnesses, I would not know whether they match him or her. Since the פסוק says 'to his brother', it means his brother and not his sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step reaches its main point. It finishes answering where the משנה gets חנק for the עדים זוממין of a בת כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the woman and the man get the same death, so it is clear what the witnesses get. A בת כהן is different: she gets שריפה, but he gets חנק. The word 'brother' (a male) tells us the witnesses match the man, so they get חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of a כהן. If she sins as a married woman, she gets burning.
Burning, one of the four court death penalties
The man who sinned with her
They are compared to, or put in the same group as
To his brother, and not to his sister

steps.whatToRemember: The עדים זוממין of a בת כהן get חנק, the man's punishment, because the פסוק says 'his brother'.
steps.confusionAlert: The witnesses do not get her punishment (שריפה), even though they spoke about her. They are matched to the man.

phrases.english: A kohen's daughter, she is punished by burning,
and the man with her is not punished by burning.
Plotting witnesses: I would not know

phrases.aramaic: אִם לוֹ הוּקְשׁוּ, אִם לָהּ הוּקְשׁוּ.
phrases.english: whether they are compared to him, or compared to her.
When the פסוק says 'to do to his brother',
phrases.notes: דברים 19:19

phrases.english: it means to his brother, and not to his sister.
phrases.notes: So the witnesses get the man's death, חנק. That is exactly what the משנה said.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״לַעֲשׂוֹת לְאָחִיו״ – לְאָחִיו וְלֹא לַאֲחוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא of רבי יוסי begun in step 15 and brings it to its point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עדים זוממין of a בת כהן are matched to the man and get חנק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's חנק for the witnesses of a בת כהן comes from 'לאחיו ולא לאחותו'.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אלו הן הנחנקין
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the פרק about the people who get חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'These are the ones who are strangled.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic of חנק is now done. The next line starts a brand-new פרק with a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. It is said when finishing a פרק.
Those who are put to death by strangling

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'These are the ones who are strangled'

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ אֵלּוּ הֵן הַנֶּחְנָקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole פרק after the last derivation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of פרק אלו הן הנחנקין.

steps.title: All of Israel have a share in the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens with a big rule: every Jew has a share in עולם הבא. It brings a פסוק from ישעיהו as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All of Israel have a share in the World to Come, as it says: 'And your people are all righteous; they will inherit the land forever; the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, to be glorified.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a new משנה. It states a general rule and backs it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule starts out wide: 'all' of ישראל. The פסוק says 'your people are all righteous' and will 'inherit the land forever', and the משנה reads this as the share in עולם הבא. Next, the משנה will list exceptions to this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. It marks the start of a new משנה.
A share or portion
The World to Come
As it is said. It introduces a פסוק.

steps.whyThisMatters: This opening line gives this פרק its famous name, פרק חלק.

phrases.english: משנה: All of Israel
have a share in the World to Come,
as it says: 'And your people are all righteous;'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 60:21

phrases.english: they will inherit the land forever;
the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to be glorified.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new פרק with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every Jew has a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: The first exceptions: people who deny basic beliefs
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists people who lose their share. One who says the Torah does not teach תחיית המתים, one who says the Torah is not from Heaven, and an אפיקורוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the ones who have no share in the World to Come: one who says resurrection of the dead is not from the Torah, one who says the Torah is not from Heaven, and an אפיקורוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the exceptions to its big rule. These are people who lose their share in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is an exception list. These people are still part of ישראל, but they lose the share that 'all of Israel' would normally have. Each one rejects a basic belief.

keyTerms.meaning: The dead coming back to life in the future
That the Torah was given by ה׳
A person who treats Torah and its scholars with contempt

steps.confusionAlert: Read the first case carefully. It is about someone who says תחיית המתים is not 'from the Torah', meaning he denies that the Torah teaches it.

phrases.english: And these are the ones who do not have
a share in the World to Come:

phrases.aramaic: הָאוֹמֵר אֵין תְּחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: one who says resurrection of the dead is not from the Torah,
and that the Torah is not from Heaven,
phrases.notes: The words 'one who says' carry over to this case too.

phrases.english: and an אפיקורוס.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lists exceptions to the general rule of step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who denies that the Torah teaches תחיית המתים, one who denies תורה מן השמים, and an אפיקורוס lose their share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא adds two more people to the list
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא adds two more people. One who reads the outside books, and one who whispers a פסוק over a wound to heal it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Also one who reads the outside books, and one who whispers over a wound and says: 'Every illness that I put on Egypt I will not put on you, for I am ה׳ your Healer.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא adds more people to the משנה's list of those with no share in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'also' (אף) shows he agrees with the first list and adds to it. His second case is using a פסוק as a healing charm over a wound.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, in addition
Outside books, which are not part of the holy books
One who whispers a charm
A wound

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אַף הַקּוֹרֵא בַּסְּפָרִים הַחִיצוֹנִים,
phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says: Also one who reads the outside books,
and one who whispers over a wound and says:
'Every illness that I put on Egypt'
phrases.notes: שמות 15:26

phrases.english: 'I will not put on you,'
'for I am ה׳, your Healer.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אַף הַקּוֹרֵא בַּסְּפָרִים הַחִיצוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more cases to the exception list of step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Also with no share: one who reads the outside books, and one who whispers a פסוק over a wound.

steps.title: אבא שאול adds one who says ה׳'s Name as it is spelled
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול adds one more person. One who pronounces ה׳'s Name using its letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: Also one who pronounces the Name with its letters.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא, אבא שאול, adds one more person to the list of those with no share in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the word 'also' shows that he adds to the list and does not argue with it. His case is saying ה׳'s Name out loud exactly as it is written.

keyTerms.meaning: One who pronounces or says out loud
ה׳'s Name
With its letters, exactly as it is written

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list of people with no share in עולם הבא now has three parts: the first list, רבי עקיבא's additions, and אבא שאול's addition.

phrases.english: אבא שאול says:
Also one who pronounces the Name with its letters.
phrases.notes: This means ה׳'s special Name, said out loud exactly as it is spelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: אַף הַהוֹגֶה אֶת הַשֵּׁם בְּאוֹתִיּוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case to the exception list after רבי עקיבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Also with no share: one who pronounces ה׳'s Name with its letters.

steps.title: Three kings and four commoners lose their share
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says three kings and four commoners have no share in עולם הבא. It names the three kings: ירבעם, אחאב, and מנשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three kings and four ordinary people have no share in the World to Come. The three kings are ירבעם, אחאב, and מנשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from types of people who lose עולם הבא to specific named people. It starts with three kings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the משנה listed kinds of beliefs and actions. Now it lists real people from תנ״ך. It gives the overall count first (3 + 4) and then names the kings.

keyTerms.meaning: Kings
Ordinary people, commoners who are not kings
First king of the northern kingdom, who set up the golden calves
King of the northern kingdom, husband of איזבל
King of יהודה, son of חזקיהו, known for idol worship

phrases.english: Three kings and four commoners
have no share in the World to Come.
The three kings:
ירבעם, אחאב, and מנשה.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה מְלָכִים וְאַרְבָּעָה הֶדְיוֹטוֹת אֵין לָהֶן חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of people who lose עולם הבא, now naming specific people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירבעם, אחאב, and מנשה have no share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says מנשה does have a share
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees about מנשה. He proves from a פסוק that ה׳ accepted מנשה's prayer and brought him back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: מנשה does have a share in the World to Come, because the פסוק says, 'He prayed to Him, and He heard his plea and brought him back to ירושלים, to his kingdom.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues that מנשה should be taken off the list, and he brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that מנשה did תשובה and ה׳ accepted his prayer. רבי יהודה reads this as proof that מנשה was forgiven completely, so he keeps his share in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: And he prayed
His plea, his request for mercy
To his kingdom

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: מְנַשֶּׁה יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: מנשה has a share in the World to Come,
as it is stated: 'And he prayed to Him, and He heard his plea,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 33:13. This is about מנשה after he was taken captive to בבל.

phrases.english: and He brought him back to ירושלים, to his kingdom.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מְנַשֶּׁה יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes one name on the list of three kings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, מנשה has a share in עולם הבא, because his prayer was accepted.

steps.title: The חכמים answer: he was returned only to his kingdom
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה's proof. The פסוק only says ה׳ brought מנשה back to his throne, not to life in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: ה׳ brought him back to his kingdom, but He did not bring him back to life in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's פסוק and show it does not prove what he wants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They read the same word, לְמַלְכוּתוֹ, very exactly. The פסוק tells us where מנשה was returned to: his kingdom in this world. It says nothing about עולם הבא, so מנשה stays on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: They said to him (the other חכמים answering)
He returned him
Life in the World to Come

phrases.english: They said to him:
He returned him to his kingdom,
but He did not return him to life in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לְמַלְכוּתוֹ הֱשִׁיבוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's proof from the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof itself. The פסוק cannot show that מנשה has עולם הבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק says only 'to his kingdom'. That is a return to worldly rule, not to a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: The four commoners
steps.stepSummary: The משנה names the four commoners who have no share: בלעם, דואג, אחיתופל, and גחזי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The four commoners are בלעם, דואג, אחיתופל, and גחזי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes back to its list and finishes it by naming the four ordinary people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the side argument about מנשה, the משנה finishes the count it gave at the start. None of these four were kings, so they are called הדיוטות.

keyTerms.meaning: The non-Jewish prophet who tried to curse בני ישראל
דואג האדומי, who informed on דוד and killed the כהנים of נוב
דוד's advisor, who joined אבשלום's rebellion
The servant of אלישע

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's full list is three kings (ירבעם, אחאב, מנשה) and four commoners (בלעם, דואג, אחיתופל, גחזי). רבי יהודה disagrees only about מנשה.

phrases.english: The four commoners:
בלעם, דואג, אחיתופל, and גחזי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבָּעָה הֶדְיוֹטוֹת: בִּלְעָם, וְדוֹאֵג, וַאֲחִיתוֹפֶל, וְגֵחֲזִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the מנשה argument to finish the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בלעם, דואג, אחיתופל, and גחזי have no share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Why such a harsh punishment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking why someone who denies that the Torah teaches תחיית המתים loses his whole share in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is he punished so severely?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens and goes back to the first case in the משנה. It asks why that person is punished so harshly, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the Torah does not teach תחיית המתים might seem like only a mistake in reading the Torah. So why lose everything? The גמרא wants the reason behind this punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the חכמים that explains the משנה
And why so much? Why such a severe result?

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the kings and commoners just listed. It goes back to the first case in the משנה: the one who denies that the Torah teaches תחיית המתים.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And why so much?
phrases.notes: This is about the person from the start of the משנה who says the Torah does not teach תחיית המתים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל כָּךְ לָמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason behind the משנה's first ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does denying that the Torah teaches תחיית המתים cost a person his whole share in עולם הבא?

steps.title: He denied it, so he will not have it: measure for measure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא answers that since he denied תחיית המתים, he will not take part in it, because ה׳ always punishes מדה כנגד מדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: He denied the resurrection of the dead, so he will have no share in the resurrection of the dead. This is because everything the Holy One, Blessed be He, does is measure for measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. The punishment fits the sin exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person denied a specific thing, תחיית המתים, and he loses exactly that thing. The punishment is not random. It is shaped to match what he did, which follows the rule of מדה כנגד מדה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (in a ברייתא)
He denied
Therefore
Measure for measure: the response matches the action

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of מדה כנגד מדה: one who denies תחיית המתים loses his own share in תחיית המתים.

phrases.english: It was taught:
He denied the resurrection of the dead,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ לֹא יִהְיֶה לוֹ חֵלֶק בִּתְחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים,
phrases.english: therefore he will have no share in the resurrection of the dead,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: since all the ways of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
are measure for measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הוּא כָּפַר בִּתְחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ punishes מדה כנגד מדה. One who denies תחיית המתים does not get to take part in it.

steps.title: Source for measure for measure: אלישע's promise
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן asks where we learn מדה כנגד מדה. He begins with אלישע's promise that food would become cheap in שמרון the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: How do we know that everything ה׳ does is measure for measure? Because the פסוק says, 'אלישע said: Hear the word of ה׳. Tomorrow at this time, a סאה of fine flour will sell for a שקל and two סאה of barley for a שקל at the gate of שמרון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the rule of מדה כנגד מדה. This step starts the story. The proof is still building and is not finished yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמרון was under siege and starving. אלישע promised that by the next day food would be very cheap. This promise is the background for the officer's doubt in the next פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
The נביא, student of אליהו
A measure of volume for grain or flour
Fine flour
The capital city of the northern kingdom

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִין שֶׁכׇּל מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: From where do we know that all the ways of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
are measure for measure?
As it is stated: 'And אלישע said: Hear the word of Hashem, etc.
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 7:1. וְגוֹ׳ means 'and so on'; it's in square brackets because the corrected wording adds it.

phrases.english: Tomorrow at this time, a סאה of fine flour for a שקל
and two סאה of barley for a שקל, at the gate of שמרון.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: מִנַּיִין שֶׁכׇּל מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source from the פסוקים for the rule used in the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that ה׳ acts מדה כנגד מדה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of אלישע and the siege of שמרון in מלכים ב פרק ז.

steps.title: The officer doubts, and is told he will see but not eat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק. The king's officer mocked אלישע's promise, and אלישע told him he would see it happen but not eat from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'The officer on whose arm the king leaned answered the man of God and said: Even if ה׳ made windows in the sky, could this happen? And he said: You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat from it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues building its proof with the second פסוק. The officer doubts ה׳'s promise and is told what will happen to him. The end of the proof comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The officer refused to believe the food would come. His punishment matches his doubt: he will see the food but not get to eat it. That is מדה כנגד מדה, just like one who denies תחיית המתים does not get to take part in it.

keyTerms.meaning: The officer, the king's high aide
The man of God, meaning אלישע
Windows or openings
But you will not eat from it

steps.whyThisMatters: The officer's case is a perfect match to the משנה. He doubted ה׳'s promise and so lost the promised good, just as one who denies תחיית המתים loses his share in it.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'And the officer answered,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 7:2

phrases.english: the one on whose arm the king leaned,
the man of God, and said:
Even if ה׳ makes windows in the sky,
could this thing happen?
And he said: You will see it with your eyes,
but you will not eat from it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּעַן הַשָּׁלִישׁ אֲשֶׁר הַמֶּלֶךְ נִשְׁעָן עַל יָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof with the next פסוק in the story.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that ה׳ acts מדה כנגד מדה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 7:2: the officer who doubted is told he will see the plenty but not eat from it.
